title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Aisha Patel
commits: a1b2c3: add initial auto-detection thresholds and detector scaffolding
d4e5f6: implement hysteresis logic and configuration parameters
1a2b3c: expose rollout guard API and admin controls
4d5e6f: add KV-cache-sensitive latency handling and tagging
7a8b9c: update docs and dashboards, add integration tests
description:
Context: We've seen a few incidents where a model rollout caused subtle latency regressions under bursty workloads because the canary detector was tuned too aggressively and lacked hysteresis and KV-cache awareness. This PR improves the perf-canary subsystem with three goals: 1) more robust automated detection of latency/throughput regressions that accounts for KV-cache warmup and batching behavior, 2) hysteresis-based thresholds to avoid flapping on short-lived spikes, and 3) stronger rollout guards and operator controls (pause, rollback, scoped throttles) to prevent noisy rollouts from impacting production traffic.

What changed: - Introduced a detector.go that computes statistical windows for latency p50/p95/p99 and request throughput and compares them against dynamic baselines derived from rolling medians. Baselines are tagged by model-version, region, and cache_hit_rate to separate cold-start/KV-cache effects. - Added hysteresis.go: a configurable hysteresis state machine (grow/hold/decay) that requires sustained deviations beyond threshold for N consecutive windows before triggering a guard. This prevents brief spikes from tripping rollouts. - Rollout guard API (handlers/rollout_guard.go): supports actions: pause-rollout, reduce-canary-traffic, rollback, and mute-alerts. Guards are annotated with reason and linked Linear/Jira keys for auditability. - Config updates (defaults.yaml): new tuning knobs: window_ms, required_windows, hysteresis_decay_ms, cache_sensitive_thresholds, min_samples, and min_rps. Default values chosen conservatively to minimize false positives. - Instrumentation: runtime/kvcache/metrics.go tags metrics with cache_hit_rate and batching_window to let the detector attribute regressions properly. Dashboards updated to show canary detector state and hysteresis stages. - Tests: added deterministic unit tests for state transitions and an integration test that replays a recorded trace with cache warmup to validate detector behavior. - CI: added an integration job that runs the canary detector against a synthetic workload to catch regressions before merging.

Why this is safe: changes are behind a feature flag (perf_canary.v2_auto_detect) and default tuning is conservative. Rollout guard actions require explicit operator confirmation for destructive actions (rollback) in Dedicated and Private deployments. No public API changes aside from a new admin endpoint for rollout control.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for hysteresis and detection logic included. - Integration test replays historical incident traces and validates that detector only alerts when regressions persist beyond configured windows. - Ran canary integration job in CI against a staging cluster; results attached. - Verified that default settings do not trigger on normal traffic profiles across our standard canary dataset.

Migration/ops notes: - Operators can enable perf_canary.v2_auto_detect via config or Console. After enabling, monitor the "Perf Canary Detector" dashboard for 24-48 hours. If you see unnecessary guard triggers, adjust cache_sensitive_thresholds and required_windows. - For Dedicated customers, rollback actions are gated and require support approval.

Related work: builds on ENG-2345 (initial canary detector prototype) and ENG-2410 (kv-cache-aware metrics). Addresses SUP-4521 which reported a canary-induced latency regression in production.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Dashboard updates - [x] Feature-flagged - [x] Release notes
review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice work — the hysteresis state machine looks sensible. Two questions: 1) did you try adaptive window sizing for very low rps canaries? 2) can we avoid tagging every metric with cache_hit_rate in high-throughput paths?

Aisha Patel: Thanks Diego. For (1) we added min_samples and min_rps to avoid noisy windows; adaptive windows were considered but deferred to a follow-up to keep this change focused. For (2) we only tag aggregated metrics emitted by the kvcache layer, not every token path; cost is negligible in our staging runs.

Priya Rao: Please add a short rollback test that simulates a canary failing and verify the guard issues a rollback action (mocked). Also add a small note in docs about how rollback is gated for dedicated/private.
Aisha Patel: Added rollback unit test and expanded docs with gated rollback note. PTAL.
Liam Chen: lgtm after nits. Consider adding a telemetry event when hysteresis transitions from hold->grow so we can build alerts on sustained regressions.
Aisha Patel: Added telemetry event perf_canary.hysteresis_transition in metrics and updated dashboard queries.
release_notes: Improves performance canary auto-detection by adding KV-cache-aware baselines, hysteresis to avoid flapping, and stronger rollout guards (pause/reduce/rollback). Feature-flagged behind perf_canary.v2_auto_detect.
